clue.text: Turn up to hold exercises, seeing little change in Russia

indicators.note: to hold says one piece wraps around and contains the other

parts.note: to cock a hat brim or an ear is to turn it up
PE is physical exercises, school gym lessons

explanation.surface: Someone turning up to do exercises notices how little small change they carry in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads like arriving, but here it is the verb for tilting a hat brim upward; 'to hold' puts the exercises inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A copeck is a Russian coin worth a hundredth of a rouble, so a small piece of change.

clue.text: Lords and ladies obliged to have pint with this fool

definitions.text: Lords and ladies obliged to have pint with this

explanation.surface: Aristocrats being forced to drink a pint with a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Lords and ladies is a wild arum plant also called cuckoo-pint, so it must 'have pint' with the answer to make its other name.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is the plant name completed by pint; the second is crazy or silly, a fool.

clue.text: Poor inn — it foolishly served no white wine

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters behaving in a mixed-up way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor-quality inn stupidly offered a wine that was not white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' is a link word between the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir is a red grape and red wine, so it is no white wine.

clue.text: A friend in service

explanation.surface: A friend who is in domestic service.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, shortened to china; a china service is a dinner set.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a pal in rhyming slang; the other is porcelain, as in a set of crockery.

clue.text: One sort of saw this letter

explanation.surface: A tool and a piece of correspondence are being described together.
explanation.walkthrough: A circular saw is one kind of saw; a circular is a letter sent round to many people, which this round letter could be.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a power saw with a spinning disc blade, and a printed letter distributed widely.

clue.text: That is the thing about some French

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: it means the thing referred to
des is French for some

explanation.surface: A remark explaining something about the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the French word inside the pronoun; the Latin phrase is usually abbreviated i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

clue.text: Artist allowed to follow wedding scene

indicators.note: follow means the pieces named first come after the scene

parts.note: Cana in Galilee is where the Bible sets the wedding at which water became wine
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A painter is allowed to come after a wedding picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' places the allowed pieces after the biblical wedding town; 'wedding scene' looks like a picture title, apt for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the Venetian painter famous for views of Venice.

clue.text: Composer heard record

indicators.note: heard means the word sounds like another word with different spelling

parts.note: to list is to record in writing

explanation.surface: A composer is heard on a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense of 'record' is a disc of music, which fits a composer; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer and pianist.

clue.text: Reviving friend in boxing venue?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: boxers fight in a ring
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend is coming round in a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a ring is only one kind of boxing venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallying means recovering strength, as a patient or a market rallies.

clue.text: Cob that can be made to hunt with zeal

indicators.note: can be made to says the letters can be worked into something else

explanation.surface: A horse that can be made to hunt keenly.
explanation.walkthrough: A cob is also a sturdy horse, which suits hunting; here it is a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob or cobnut is a type of hazelnut.

clue.text: One hoping to be chosen, is girl able to go out with boys?

parts.note: to be able is to can, as in 'I can'
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
to date is to go out with someone romantically, here boys

explanation.surface: A question about whether a girl is allowed to date boys yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: CAN first, then DI, then DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate stands for election or selection, hoping to be picked.

clue.text: Space agency adds length in the nozzle

parts.note: NASA is the American space agency

explanation.surface: A space agency fits extra length to a rocket nozzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nozzle' is slang for the nose, so the definition means relating to the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means of or in the nose, and nozzle is a jokey word for the nose.

clue.text: Crustless cob batch taken for something like a biscuit

indicators.note: crustless means each word loses its outer layer, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Bread rolls from a batch have had their crusts cut off for a biscuit-like snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Cob and batch are both British words for loaves or rolls, which steers the solver towards bread. Their insides, O, ATC and AKE, join up.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a flat savoury oat biscuit, so it is something like a biscuit.

clue.text: Author of play on Westward channel

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it comes after it
westward in an across clue means read right to left, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a slot is a narrow channel or groove
to toy is to play

explanation.surface: Sounds like a credit for a play broadcast on the Westward television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Westward was a regional ITV company in south-west England, so it looks like a TV channel; 'Westward' really turns the channel word backwards, and 'on' puts the play word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace.

clue.text: Had long trip — ten circuits here?

definitions.text: Had long trip — ten circuits here?

indicators.note: circuits suggests going round and round, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot complains of a long flight that circled ten times before landing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a plane stuck in a stack might do ten laps on a long trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A holding pattern is the oval route aircraft fly while waiting for permission to land.

clue.text: Ship which is likely to break down

definitions.text: which is likely to break down

explanation.surface: A ship that is likely to break down.
explanation.walkthrough: A destroyer is a fast warship; also something that breaks things down.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a warship; the other is anything that wrecks or demolishes.

clue.text: Bearing gifts, but rough-spoken

indicators.note: rough-spoken says the word, roughly pronounced, sounds like the answer

parts.note: presents are gifts

explanation.surface: Someone carrying gifts but speaking coarsely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like carrying, but it means carriage or demeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence and bearing both mean a person's dignified manner or air.

clue.text: Derby rail works being the first to start in the morning

definitions.text: the first to start in the morning

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Engineering works on a railway at Derby begin first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English railway town, which makes 'works' look like a rail works.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bird is someone who gets up and starts work early.

clue.text: Bliss is to be found in shops

indicators.note: to be found in places one piece inside another

parts.note: in Britain a parade is a row of shops
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper finds happiness among the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: A parade of shops is a short row of shops along a street, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise means perfect happiness, a state of bliss.

clue.text: Going over the ship's side, generally

parts.note: across means going over from one side to the other
taken as written
board is an old word for the side of a ship, as in overboard

explanation.surface: Someone goes over the side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone climbing overboard; 'generally' is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the board is an idiom meaning applying to everyone or everything, in general.

clue.text: One in a hundred? Just the reverse, right now

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another
Just the reverse says the clue's order is swapped, so the second piece holds the first

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards
a ton is a hundred

explanation.surface: A question about odds of one in a hundred, then a demand to flip it at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, 'One in a hundred' would put the card word inside the hundred word; 'Just the reverse' swaps that, so the hundred goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: At once is an idiom meaning immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Stopped short to look with pleasure at a large butterfly

indicators.note: stopped short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to admire something is to look at it with pleasure
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone stops suddenly to gaze happily at a big butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: ADMIRE without its last letter E gives ADMIR, then A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral is a common European butterfly.

clue.text: Court pursues obstinate person endlessly for swindle

indicators.note: pursues means this piece follows the other
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mule is a stubborn person

explanation.surface: A court goes after a stubborn person for fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the stubborn animal, and 'pursues' puts the court abbreviation after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mulct is to extract money by fraud, to fleece or swindle.

clue.text: Loch — or lake, in fact

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
even is an intensifier meaning indeed or in fact

explanation.surface: Is it a loch or really a lake?
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Leven is in Kinross, Scotland, where Mary, Queen of Scots was held.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Leven is a well-known Scottish freshwater loch.

clue.text: Obscure significance apparent in French tomb

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a crypt is an underground tomb or vault

explanation.surface: Some hidden meaning shows itself in a tomb in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparent' just links the definition to the wordplay that shows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt is to put a message into code, hiding its meaning.

clue.text: Small farm back in court for cheating

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small farmer is back in court for cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run of letters across 'court for cheating'; reading TFORC backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: One succeeded getting stake in Scottish island

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
to lay is to stake a bet

explanation.surface: A person inherits a stake in a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, known for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is one of the islands of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland.

clue.text: Morally strict in part of Australia

explanation.surface: Puritan attitudes found somewhere in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19th-century era of Queen Victoria is known for strict morals; Victoria is also an Australian state, whose people are Victorians.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense describes prim nineteenth-century values; the other means belonging to the state of Victoria.

clue.text: Do this? One then maybe has king in place

definitions.text: Do this? One then maybe has king in place

indicators.note: in place says the king's letter is set inside the rearranged letters
maybe signals that the letters of these words could be arranged differently

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what to do so that a king ends up installed.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged ONE THEN takes R inside it. 'Do this?' points to the whole clue as the definition: having a king put in place is what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthrone a monarch is to seat them on the throne, putting a king in place.

clue.text: Stumped by poem about good solid food

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around another

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a poem about hearty food.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter is stumped when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground; scorers write ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food such as suet pudding.
